+ line-by-line
- Hide text

a perfect cover to slip the militias sent out to keep order

I don't think "militia" is really the term you want here.

scuttling behind the back of an unsuspecting mercenary

I also don't think "mercenary" makes a lot of sense here.

The man was spraying boiling lead into a crowd of orange jumpsuit wearing men and women,

So I'm confused here. Is the guard literally spraying liquid, molten lead onto people as some sort of bizarre, anomalous anti-riot measure? Is this a euphemism for shooting people? At first I thought it was some skip who could shoot molten lead at people. I'm not really sure what you're going for here.

A firecracker with a bit of metal stuck on it, jettisoned down a tube.

So I guess it is a euphemism for shooting a gun. So why is the lead "boiling"?

“I've gotta keep a clear head,” the object thought to himself.

So the protagonist of this story is an extradimensional being who is so different from humans that it finds them horrifying. Stuff like this kind of works at cross-purposes to that theme, because it sounds just like some guy talking here. I also found the character thinking literal quotations to himself a little choppy in terms of style.

The gentle sound of a crack and a scream

I don't know that I would describe the sound of SCP-173 snapping necks as "gentle".

his sensitive sensory organ

"Sensitive sensory" feels repetitive here.

who was unable to do anything but swear worse than any sailor

Eyepod-beings have sailors in their home dimension? Who have the same idiosyncracies as sailors here do? Really?

I feel like that, much the same as SCP-682, there's enough SCP-173 material on the site now, if not too much. Because of that, I as an individual reader really need to be taken aback to support an article with those skips in them. I know that the Eyepods are the main focus, but it's still a pretty integral part of the story.

That issue is compounded by the execution issues listed above. There was an attempt to adopt an alien perspective, which can be interesting (albeit tricky to accomplish), but that perspective was either too inconsistent or too close to a normal human to really convey the feeling that should come with adopting the mindset of something completely non-human.

I also don't understand why the Eyepod stops to help contain 173. 173 didn't seem to pose any risk to the Eyepod, since it was rushing past it in order to find more human necks to snap. So given that the protagonist wants nothing more than to be free and hates its captors, what sense is there in stopping an escape attempt, of something that is hindering its enemies?
